title_original: 《女籃巨人烏莉亞》：競技之外的暈眩與其他
title_zh: 《女籃巨人烏莉亞》：競技之外的暈眩與其他
summary_zh: 来源摘录：在故事的大多階段，我們接收到的重心首先是普世問題：關於一個人物，之於她所身處環境的格格不入，但在故事之外，演員的性別身分與詮釋，仍在許多時刻出現（無關乎在或不在電影預設之內）關於性別的觀看效果。我們要如何理解眼前所見的，遭遇特定身體處境的人物，她的性別與「性」為何，她的社會互動與身體，存在什麼特徵？ 這篇文章 《女籃巨人烏莉亞》：競技之外的暈眩與其他 最早出現於 釀電影 。

Kairish）新作《女籃巨人烏莉亞》（Ulya）入選今年坎城影展「一種注目」單元，電影的時間背景設定在 1964 年，描述拉脫維亞籃球傳奇人物烏莉安娜・謝米諾娃（Uļjana Semjonova，1952－2026）生涯早期的生活。", "links": [{"text": "2026 高雄電影節「非典型視窗」單元", "url": "https://filmaholic.tw/editors/6ac698f6fd89780001aa6fd4/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "電影並非以一段特定的成就或競賽經驗著手，而著重在烏莉亞接觸籃球的早期背景：出身於傳統的俄羅斯舊禮儀派農民家庭，宗教、族群與蘇聯六〇年代的政治氛圍縈繞在電影敘事中，青少女離開貧窮的生長環境，進入一個能夠改變她生涯的教育與職業環境。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在傳記故事的色彩中，這些改變都被已經寫定的現實所許諾，必定會發生；儘管有著明確可操作的戲劇化成長故事基調，但《女籃巨人烏莉亞》並不將重心放在她的成就，它更多是一個身處自我懷疑的階段，對生活（而非競賽）充滿挫敗感的青少年敘事。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/Qx_uPgG00xJJzg6WiCziG7EbHuqwwIU8Uh8l57W68-Y/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/3109793d-b790-4c82-8fbe-fd02bcfa5646.jpg", "alt": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "電影的共同編劇之一，同時是演出烏莉亞（Ulya）的主要演員 Karlis Arnolds Avots，在作品成形的過程中扮演重要的位置。自承深受烏莉亞所影響，《女籃巨人烏莉亞》的劇本發想由 Karlis Arnolds Avots 本人開始，且最早就設定為由他親自主演的作品。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Karlis Arnolds Avots 原先是劇場演員，他與導演凱里斯從劇場開始合作； 在劇場，由男性演員演出女性角色，有較明確的傳統可供依循，而他嘗試在電影裡實現這個構想，且是面對一個在當地幾近家喻戶曉的真實人物，並非採用象徵手法，而以嚴肅且接近寫實的背景設計來詮釋她。 無可避免地，這個決策會為電影增加話題與爭議性，尤其關於女性身分的代表性問題。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "若單純以作品呈現來看，一個由現實 30 歲上下的成年男性所詮釋的 16 歲青少女，Karlis Arnolds Avots 並未主張自己在生理或性別認同上跨越這些界線，而更多是嘗試以普世性的情感，去看待這名角色身處的困難。 《女籃巨人烏莉亞》最主要被突顯的人物特色，是烏莉亞對身體的不安，高大且壯碩的骨架讓她成為球探的目標，卻也因此與社群環境產生疏離感。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在角色的描繪上，Karlis Arnolds Avots 加強揣摩這種無法融入群體的肢體特徵，烏莉亞的形象顯得害羞或侷促，而她在球場上的反應有時看起來笨拙且不自信，而這些不自信並非是以技巧、天賦成長的成敗所衡量，更在於故事對她心理狀態的側重：她對她的身體保有疑惑。 在故事呈現中，這種疑惑的重心不完全關於性別，但因為觀眾注視著一個成年男性的、非依靠象徵處理的表演，這種不安便有了多重的理解空間和聯想。"}, {"type": "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "烏莉亞所體會的，不僅只是一般青春故事的內心疏離，她與他人無法融入的困惑，多方向地在宗教、族群、經濟狀況與體格等現實狀況上感到不安。我們看到一個青少女倍受煎熬，電影中亦提及球員身分的荷爾蒙檢測，或是表現警員以檢查生殖器的粗暴做法臨檢其性別身分，然而這些情節並未出現明確的現實落點，許多時候，它們僅是呼應著作為故事背景的蘇聯社會與時代氛圍。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在故事的大多階段，我們接收到的重心首先是普世問題：關於一個人物，之於她所身處環境的格格不入，但在故事之外，演員的性別身分與詮釋，仍在許多時刻出現（無關乎在或不在電影預設之內）關於性別的觀看效果。 我們要如何理解眼前所見的，遭遇特定身體處境的人物，她的性別與「性」為何，她的社會互動與身體，存在什麼特徵？又，為何這些特徵是重要的，真實的烏莉亞對身體的不安是否能與之類比？而再一次，這個類比能否建立，本身又是重要的嗎？這些問題據此往下綿延，並不容易在作品本身獲得解答。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在關於性別的判斷之外，導演凱里斯與曾獲柏林影展銀熊獎肯定的攝影指導沃傑赫・斯大隆（Wojciech Staron），共同在電影形式上加強了烏莉亞內外掙扎的角色狀態。電影以 4：3 的景框、黑白攝影呈現，準確且節制。 形式嚴密地控制故事訊息，位處在景框內的人物時常是模糊的，或處在焦距之外；極端且高亮度的光線、遮掩的門框或牆板，或單純因為身處於主觀之中，而無法得見全觀的視覺印象。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "故事時常呼應烏莉亞當下的情緒判斷，觀眾大多時候都在僅有部分可見的位置中經驗故事，而透過與旁人的對比，我們會反覆看到烏莉亞高大的身形，在構圖中反覆顯得突兀而難以親近。 當她離家、與同儕沐浴，或單純在球場上感到暈眩，這些情緒並非直接透過烏莉亞的視線為主觀鏡頭的呈現，但仍改變觀眾觀看到故事的方式。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/n7bGRM0FYGVWBP5w4OFopqkYNirw9ZvankUf1mdZfUU/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/b0c3b257-43a5-44d7-95d2-1022de6752b7.jpg", "alt": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/zPGWfivfJbDGIX64Dik5MgyzBIyN_YofISkIcu6BVAs/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/eac89bd5-9d22-49ba-abf2-2a9a08816d0e.jpg", "alt": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "對於角色內心狀態的視覺刻劃，並不完全透過表演或情節對白來傳達。這是本片從一般的競技運動敘事中轉向的方式，比起運動本身的輸或贏，甚至是這些輸贏如何影響身處在運動中的人物，《女籃巨人烏莉亞》關心的似乎更是一個，在運動上顯現天賦、突出於常人的人，在一個並不穩定的環境裡，更可能處於何種生活狀態。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "烏莉亞同時身處在她的青春期，在與同儕並不相容的語言與宗教，在一個評判她身體價值的競技系統，也在六〇年代蘇聯的政治氛圍之中。 電影並未以任何一者決斷她的掙扎，角色關鍵的動作或選擇時常保持留白，我們不常見到巨大的情緒性爭執。這個做法保全了這部電影冷靜且專注的敘事策略，但偶爾讓人懷疑，我們是否是在一個虛構的人物故事當中，試圖尋得移情理解，而非真實地觀測一個具體發生過的事件。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "烏莉亞大多時候都身處邊緣，與自己的欲望共處。故事在一個複雜的社會背景中，處理著相對單純的青春期困惑，對群體歸屬或是親密關係的朦朧欲望。 這些欲望是電影主要的情緒來源，而在故事的尾段，匱乏的人際連結、對親密關係的想像，連結到她身為明日之星的競技「價值」，則對她產生另一次衝擊。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "劇本在此處活用了這個明確的戲劇化場景，表現教練與隊友們，對於烏莉亞在電影中段已有前例的不知所蹤感到不安，而最後她卻自行度過這個困境。 隨之而來的答案是，在這些波折發生時，她已經跟她的天賦建立了更緊密的精神連結，這個連結如今足以保護她。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/JBdKrU59Q8556O764K3EO-7wdLI98JMx2S5V9I5XR8k/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/40d47ff4-4790-43bb-87c3-97c89ed81d60.jpg", "alt": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/dsAGKTvnzLvrgvbR86EqQTilGI7jhrn9bI03XyVWUuU/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/75391c6f-8faa-46e1-8485-a66266d8505a.jpg", "alt": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「籃球」在此處因此扮演著有趣的角色，不在球場上，而在球場下。這是許多競技運動電影偶爾會提出，但不常被視為主軸的觀點。超過競技現場的五感，或反覆自我拷問的技藝、勝負、功利磨練過程，運動在此回歸為個人精神方面的避風港。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自然而然地，它關於「你的個人天賦（特質），與隨之而來的努力，會在某個時刻拯救你」，但它發生作用的時間點，並不在眾人從旁看到的一刻，甚至不盡然是電影選擇呈現給觀眾看到的一刻。 《女籃巨人烏莉亞》在此處選擇一條更單純的角度，去觀看人物的故事，有時候我們稱其為平靜，而在平靜之外的事情，都發生在故事之外。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/0QxoHwODs_iUzwQKwYdVGR_-ihYbyalXxk156y3gFgQ/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/ad106457-671f-48b1-ae43-2596da87a46a.jpg", "alt": "《釀電影》熱天午後——𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 高雄電影節專題／圖像提供：釀電影", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《釀電影》熱天午後——𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 高雄電影節專題／圖像提供：釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "將於 2026 年 10 月 09 日正式開展的 2026 高雄電影節，以獨樹一格的選片視角與具爆發力的影像能量，持續撞擊當代觀影體驗的既定邊界。《釀電影》編輯室以「熱天午後」為策展專題，延伸自希臘導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）的短片代表作《雅典熱天午後》（Washingtonia，2014），連結柯薩瑪尼系列作品的城市、荒塚與冷酷異境。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本次專題將由獨立評論人黃曦與導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）進行深度訪談，藉由系譜性地閱讀柯薩瑪尼，觀眾方能照見導演從植物、自然科學與傳頌百年的神話中，刺向當代社會的體制、階級、語言等困境，由此提出一道粉嫩且霓虹的提問；與此同時，本專題亦同步收錄獨立評論人沈怡昕於坎城影展現場，與柯薩瑪尼圍繞新作《人魚戀習曲》（Titanic Ocean，2026）之對答集。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在本屆的「非典型視窗」單元片單，則集結 11 部來自世界各地的當代作品，此次專題將分別聚焦四部作品進行評論分析。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其中包括，獨立評論人許騰云剖析曾以《愛情美樂地》（Joyland，2022）獲該屆坎城影展「一種注目單元」評審團大獎的巴基斯坦導演沙馬．蘇丹．庫薩特（Sarmad Sultan Khoosat），透過同為古典寓言的新作《新婚美樂地》（Lali），呈示喧騰、荒唐的禮讚與喪鐘，以及傳統婚姻制度下的女性宿命。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾任多年記者，現為文字工作者的阿潑（島嶼無風帶）帶領讀者走進韓國名導鄭智泳（정지영）新作《我的名字是⋯》（My Name），嘗試穿梭於當代校園、近代歷史之間，回顧被巨大歷史洪流所掩埋的「濟州四・三事件」（제주 4・3 사건）。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "獨立評論人蔡曉松則著眼改編自女籃球星烏莉安娜．謝米諾娃（Uļjana Semjonova）真實故事、拉脫維亞導演維斯圖爾．凱里斯（Viesturs Kairišs）於新作《女籃巨人烏莉亞》（Ulya）呈現的特異、詩意的鏡頭與表演呈現。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最後，由獨立評論人桑妮執筆法國邪典導演貝特朗．曼迪科（Bertrand Mandico）新作《羅馬瘋情畫》，探究一代名導如何攜手奧斯卡影后瑪莉詠．柯蒂亞（Marion Cotillard）與《燃燒女子的畫像》（Portrait de la jeune fille en feu，2019）諾耶米．梅蘭特（Noémie Merlant），在情色食人科幻狂想中，以鉛黃電影與費里尼式的怪誕拼貼，交出當代垃圾美學與女性主義謝幕的迷人花火。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，《釀電影》編輯室也將於影展期間走訪高雄電影節，進行其他短篇評論分析：「年度主題：抓馬人間」單元之《飛瀑怒潮》（Niagara，1953）、《夢魘人妻》（DreamQuil，2026）；「多倫多亞洲電影節精選」單元之《海草之家》（Seagrass，2023）、《世界上最ㄅㄧㄤˋ的國家》（The Greatest Country in the World，2019）；「抓馬跨世代單元：阿莫多瓦 article_text:
撰文／蔡曉松 劇照提供／高雄電影節 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦

2026 高雄電影節「非典型視窗」單元 ，拉脫維亞導演維斯圖爾・凱里斯（Viestur Kairish）新作《女籃巨人烏莉亞》（Ulya）入選今年坎城影展「一種注目」單元，電影的時間背景設定在 1964 年，描述拉脫維亞籃球傳奇人物烏莉安娜・謝米諾娃（Uļjana Semjonova，1952－2026）生涯早期的生活。

電影並非以一段特定的成就或競賽經驗著手，而著重在烏莉亞接觸籃球的早期背景：出身於傳統的俄羅斯舊禮儀派農民家庭，宗教、族群與蘇聯六〇年代的政治氛圍縈繞在電影敘事中，青少女離開貧窮的生長環境，進入一個能夠改變她生涯的教育與職業環境。

在傳記故事的色彩中，這些改變都被已經寫定的現實所許諾，必定會發生；儘管有著明確可操作的戲劇化成長故事基調，但《女籃巨人烏莉亞》並不將重心放在她的成就，它更多是一個身處自我懷疑的階段，對生活（而非競賽）充滿挫敗感的青少年敘事。

《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節

電影的共同編劇之一，同時是演出烏莉亞（Ulya）的主要演員 Karlis Arnolds Avots，在作品成形的過程中扮演重要的位置。自承深受烏莉亞所影響，《女籃巨人烏莉亞》的劇本發想由 Karlis Arnolds Avots 本人開始，且最早就設定為由他親自主演的作品。

Karlis Arnolds Avots 原先是劇場演員，他與導演凱里斯從劇場開始合作； 在劇場，由男性演員演出女性角色，有較明確的傳統可供依循，而他嘗試在電影裡實現這個構想，且是面對一個在當地幾近家喻戶曉的真實人物，並非採用象徵手法，而以嚴肅且接近寫實的背景設計來詮釋她。 無可避免地，這個決策會為電影增加話題與爭議性，尤其關於女性身分的代表性問題。

若單純以作品呈現來看，一個由現實 30 歲上下的成年男性所詮釋的 16 歲青少女，Karlis Arnolds Avots 並未主張自己在生理或性別認同上跨越這些界線，而更多是嘗試以普世性的情感，去看待這名角色身處的困難。 《女籃巨人烏莉亞》最主要被突顯的人物特色，是烏莉亞對身體的不安，高大且壯碩的骨架讓她成為球探的目標，卻也因此與社群環境產生疏離感。

在角色的描繪上，Karlis Arnolds Avots 加強揣摩這種無法融入群體的肢體特徵，烏莉亞的形象顯得害羞或侷促，而她在球場上的反應有時看起來笨拙且不自信，而這些不自信並非是以技巧、天賦成長的成敗所衡量，更在於故事對她心理狀態的側重：她對她的身體保有疑惑。 在故事呈現中，這種疑惑的重心不完全關於性別，但因為觀眾注視著一個成年男性的、非依靠象徵處理的表演，這種不安便有了多重的理解空間和聯想。

《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節

《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節

烏莉亞所體會的，不僅只是一般青春故事的內心疏離，她與他人無法融入的困惑，多方向地在宗教、族群、經濟狀況與體格等現實狀況上感到不安。我們看到一個青少女倍受煎熬，電影中亦提及球員身分的荷爾蒙檢測，或是表現警員以檢查生殖器的粗暴做法臨檢其性別身分，然而這些情節並未出現明確的現實落點，許多時候，它們僅是呼應著作為故事背景的蘇聯社會與時代氛圍。

在故事的大多階段，我們接收到的重心首先是普世問題：關於一個人物，之於她所身處環境的格格不入，但在故事之外，演員的性別身分與詮釋，仍在許多時刻出現（無關乎在或不在電影預設之內）關於性別的觀看效果。 我們要如何理解眼前所見的，遭遇特定身體處境的人物，她的性別與「性」為何，她的社會互動與身體，存在什麼特徵？又，為何這些特徵是重要的，真實的烏莉亞對身體的不安是否能與之類比？而再一次，這個類比能否建立，本身又是重要的嗎？這些問題據此往下綿延，並不容易在作品本身獲得解答。

在關於性別的判斷之外，導演凱里斯與曾獲柏林影展銀熊獎肯定的攝影指導沃傑赫・斯大隆（Wojciech Staron），共同在電影形式上加強了烏莉亞內外掙扎的角色狀態。電影以 4：3 的景框、黑白攝影呈現，準確且節制。 形式嚴密地控制故事訊息，位處在景框內的人物時常是模糊的，或處在焦距之外；極端且高亮度的光線、遮掩的門框或牆板，或單純因為身處於主觀之中，而無法得見全觀的視覺印象。

故事時常呼應烏莉亞當下的情緒判斷，觀眾大多時候都在僅有部分可見的位置中經驗故事，而透過與旁人的對比，我們會反覆看到烏莉亞高大的身形，在構圖中反覆顯得突兀而難以親近。 當她離家、與同儕沐浴，或單純在球場上感到暈眩，這些情緒並非直接透過烏莉亞的視線為主觀鏡頭的呈現，但仍改變觀眾觀看到故事的方式。

《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節

《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節

對於角色內心狀態的視覺刻劃，並不完全透過表演或情節對白來傳達。這是本片從一般的競技運動敘事中轉向的方式，比起運動本身的輸或贏，甚至是這些輸贏如何影響身處在運動中的人物，《女籃巨人烏莉亞》關心的似乎更是一個，在運動上顯現天賦、突出於常人的人，在一個並不穩定的環境裡，更可能處於何種生活狀態。

烏莉亞同時身處在她的青春期，在與同儕並不相容的語言與宗教，在一個評判她身體價值的競技系統，也在六〇年代蘇聯的政治氛圍之中。 電影並未以任何一者決斷她的掙扎，角色關鍵的動作或選擇時常保持留白，我們不常見到巨大的情緒性爭執。這個做法保全了這部電影冷靜且專注的敘事策略，但偶爾讓人懷疑，我們是否是在一個虛構的人物故事當中，試圖尋得移情理解，而非真實地觀測一個具體發生過的事件。

烏莉亞大多時候都身處邊緣，與自己的欲望共處。故事在一個複雜的社會背景中，處理著相對單純的青春期困惑，對群體歸屬或是親密關係的朦朧欲望。 這些欲望是電影主要的情緒來源，而在故事的尾段，匱乏的人際連結、對親密關係的想像，連結到她身為明日之星的競技「價值」，則對她產生另一次衝擊。

劇本在此處活用了這個明確的戲劇化場景，表現教練與隊友們，對於烏莉亞在電影中段已有前例的不知所蹤感到不安，而最後她卻自行度過這個困境。 隨之而來的答案是，在這些波折發生時，她已經跟她的天賦建立了更緊密的精神連結，這個連結如今足以保護她。

《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節

《女籃巨人烏莉亞》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節

「籃球」在此處因此扮演著有趣的角色，不在球場上，而在球場下。這是許多競技運動電影偶爾會提出，但不常被視為主軸的觀點。超過競技現場的五感，或反覆自我拷問的技藝、勝負、功利磨練過程，運動在此回歸為個人精神方面的避風港。

自然而然地，它關於「你的個人天賦（特質），與隨之而來的努力，會在某個時刻拯救你」，但它發生作用的時間點，並不在眾人從旁看到的一刻，甚至不盡然是電影選擇呈現給觀眾看到的一刻。 《女籃巨人烏莉亞》在此處選擇一條更單純的角度，去觀看人物的故事，有時候我們稱其為平靜，而在平靜之外的事情，都發生在故事之外。

《釀電影》熱天午後——𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 高雄電影節專題／圖像提供：釀電影

將於 2026 年 10 月 09 日正式開展的 2026 高雄電影節，以獨樹一格的選片視角與具爆發力的影像能量，持續撞擊當代觀影體驗的既定邊界。《釀電影》編輯室以「熱天午後」為策展專題，延伸自希臘導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）的短片代表作《雅典熱天午後》（Washingtonia，2014），連結柯薩瑪尼系列作品的城市、荒塚與冷酷異境。

本次專題將由獨立評論人黃曦與導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）進行深度訪談，藉由系譜性地閱讀柯薩瑪尼，觀眾方能照見導演從植物、自然科學與傳頌百年的神話中，刺向當代社會的體制、階級、語言等困境，由此提出一道粉嫩且霓虹的提問；與此同時，本專題亦同步收錄獨立評論人沈怡昕於坎城影展現場，與柯薩瑪尼圍繞新作《人魚戀習曲》（Titanic Ocean，2026）之對答集。

在本屆的「非典型視窗」單元片單，則集結 11 部來自世界各地的當代作品，此次專題將分別聚焦四部作品進行評論分析。

其中包括，獨立評論人許騰云剖析曾以《愛情美樂地》（Joyland，2022）獲該屆坎城影展「一種注目單元」評審團大獎的巴基斯坦導演沙馬．蘇丹．庫薩特（Sarmad Sultan Khoosat），透過同為古典寓言的新作《新婚美樂地》（Lali），呈示喧騰、荒唐的禮讚與喪鐘，以及傳統婚姻制度下的女性宿命。

曾任多年記者，現為文字工作者的阿潑（島嶼無風帶）帶領讀者走進韓國名導鄭智泳（정지영）新作《我的名字是⋯》（My Name），嘗試穿梭於當代校園、近代歷史之間，回顧被巨大歷史洪流所掩埋的「濟州四・三事件」（제주 4・3 사건）。

獨立評論人蔡曉松則著眼改編自女籃球星烏莉安娜．謝米諾娃（Uļjana Semjonova）真實故事、拉脫維亞導演維斯圖爾．凱里斯（Viesturs Kairišs）於新作《女籃巨人烏莉亞》（Ulya）呈現的特異、詩意的鏡頭與表演呈現。

最後，由獨立評論人桑妮執筆法國邪典導演貝特朗．曼迪科（Bertrand Mandico）新作《羅馬瘋情畫》，探究一代名導如何攜手奧斯卡影后瑪莉詠．柯蒂亞（Marion Cotillard）與《燃燒女子的畫像》（Portrait de la jeune fille en feu，2019）諾耶米．梅蘭特（Noémie Merlant），在情色食人科幻狂想中，以鉛黃電影與費里尼式的怪誕拼貼，交出當代垃圾美學與女性主義謝幕的迷人花火。

此外，《釀電影》編輯室也將於影展期間走訪高雄電影節，進行其他短篇評論分析：「年度主題：抓馬人間」單元之《飛瀑怒潮》（Niagara，1953）、《夢魘人妻》（DreamQuil，2026）；「多倫多亞洲電影節精選」單元之《海草之家》（Seagrass，2023）、《世界上最ㄅㄧㄤˋ的國家》（The Greatest Country in the World，2019）；「抓馬跨世代單元：阿莫多瓦 vs 哈維爾雙人組」單元之《黑球》（The Black Ball，2026）；「大銀幕必看經典」單元之《深深腥紅 導演版》（Deep Crimson Director's Cut）；「耽美主義」單元之《青春抹世物語》（What We Saw）；「特別放映」單元之《1949》（Fatherland，2026）。

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Tanzanian filmmaker Neema Ngelime’s “The Ones With the Tempered Flowers,” Palestinian director Fitnat Waked’s “On the Sea Road” and “Where Do I Belong?,” from Sudanese director Ibrahim “Snoopy” Ahmad, were among the big winners at this year’s Durban FilmMart , which wrapped with an award ceremony on Monday night.", "links": [{"text": "Durban FilmMart", "url": "https://variety.com/t/durban-filmmart/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ngelime’s directorial debut took home five awards, including the prize for best non-fiction film from South Africa’s National Film and Video Foundation and awards from DOK Leipzig, Sheffield Doc Fest and Visions du Réel. The film tells the story of a woman studying her body’s relationship to self and society, and the political weight placed on women’s bodies in Tanzania, and challenging duty masked as love."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Related Stories"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Japan-IP-market-Cannes.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "Japan IP Market Cannes", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues", "links": [{"text": "Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/japan-ip-market-returns-cannes-2027-1236933952/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/TMO_CONFERENCIA-DE-PRENSA-a-Guillermo-del-Toro.-ENTREGA-DE-MEDALLA-Filmoteca-de-la-UNAM_DANNACABALLERO-2_0.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "(l-r) Daniela Michel, Guillermo del Toro, UNAM's Jorge Martínez Micher and Hugo Alejandro Concha", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’", "links": [{"text": "Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/guillermo-del-toro-pans-labyrinth-morelia-film-festival-1236917004/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Where Do I Belong?” is the latest from Ahmad, who co-directed last year’s Sundance-premiering documentary “Khartoum.” The winner of four prizes at the DFM forum, it follows the director as he decides to leave Nairobi and return to his family in the Sudanese capital, combining documentary footage and hand-drawn pencil animation to tell an intimate and unconventional road movie. Also taking four awards was “On the Sea Road,” the debut feature from Waked, a documentary about the friendship forged between two Palestinian women separated by borders."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Among other standout projects was “The Boy Who Spoke Static,” from Nigeria’s Agbajowo Collective, the filmmaking group behind the 2024 Toronto premiere “The Legend of the Vagabond Queen of Lagos,” which won three prizes, including the prize for best fiction film from South Africa’s NFVF."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The ceremony capped a rousing edition of the pitch and finance forum at the DFM, which kicked off its 17th edition with a celebration of DFM alumnus “Ben’Imana,” from first-time Rwandan filmmaker Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo, which won the Cámera d’Or in Cannes and became that country’s first ever submission in the Oscar category for best international feature film."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Durban FilmMart Institute director Magdalene Reddy praised the “dynamic array of filmmakers and industry leaders” taking part in this year’s event and stressed how “the talent showcased in this year’s program and film projects exemplifies the strength of African cinema."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The Durban FilmMart Institute…remains committed to building the industry,” she said. “Thank you for participating with such passion and professionalism in all the programs presented over the last four days. Thank you for connecting, for telling your stories. And thank you for shifting the world with us.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Thirty-nine awards were handed out on Monday night, with a value totaling north of $120,000. article_text:
Tanzanian filmmaker Neema Ngelime’s “The Ones With the Tempered Flowers,” Palestinian director Fitnat Waked’s “On the Sea Road” and “Where Do I Belong?,” from Sudanese director Ibrahim “Snoopy” Ahmad, were among the big winners at this year’s Durban FilmMart , which wrapped with an award ceremony on Monday night.

Ngelime’s directorial debut took home five awards, including the prize for best non-fiction film from South Africa’s National Film and Video Foundation and awards from DOK Leipzig, Sheffield Doc Fest and Visions du Réel. The film tells the story of a woman studying her body’s relationship to self and society, and the political weight placed on women’s bodies in Tanzania, and challenging duty masked as love.

Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues

Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’

“Where Do I Belong?” is the latest from Ahmad, who co-directed last year’s Sundance-premiering documentary “Khartoum.” The winner of four prizes at the DFM forum, it follows the director as he decides to leave Nairobi and return to his family in the Sudanese capital, combining documentary footage and hand-drawn pencil animation to tell an intimate and unconventional road movie. Also taking four awards was “On the Sea Road,” the debut feature from Waked, a documentary about the friendship forged between two Palestinian women separated by borders.

Among other standout projects was “The Boy Who Spoke Static,” from Nigeria’s Agbajowo Collective, the filmmaking group behind the 2024 Toronto premiere “The Legend of the Vagabond Queen of Lagos,” which won three prizes, including the prize for best fiction film from South Africa’s NFVF.

The ceremony capped a rousing edition of the pitch and finance forum at the DFM, which kicked off its 17th edition with a celebration of DFM alumnus “Ben’Imana,” from first-time Rwandan filmmaker Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo, which won the Cámera d’Or in Cannes and became that country’s first ever submission in the Oscar category for best international feature film.

Durban FilmMart Institute director Magdalene Reddy praised the “dynamic array of filmmakers and industry leaders” taking part in this year’s event and stressed how “the talent showcased in this year’s program and film projects exemplifies the strength of African cinema.

“The Durban FilmMart Institute…remains committed to building the industry,” she said. “Thank you for participating with such passion and professionalism in all the programs presented over the last four days. Thank you for connecting, for telling your stories. And thank you for shifting the world with us.”

Mit sechs (!) geförderten Künstlerateliers begann im Jahr 1993 das, was mittlerweile Arbeitsraumprogramm (ARP) des Berliner Senats heißt und nicht nur Räume für bildende Künstlerinnen und Künstler, sondern auch für andere Kreative umfasst. Im Jahr darauf, dem ersten vollen Haushaltsjahr, waren es dann schon 79, und bis Mitte 2004 stieg die Zahl der Studios auf 365. Zu diesem Zeitpunkt gab die Senatskulturverwaltung die Zahlen und den sagenhaften Zuwachs durchaus mit Stolz bekannt.

Mittlerweile aber ist es mit dem Stolz vorbei, und die Senatsverwaltung hält sich bedeckt. Derzeit herrscht allerdings jene politisch sedierte Zeit zwischen den Berliner Wahlen und der Bildung eines neuen Senats, in der nichts mehr entschieden und bewegt wird. In der auch nicht entschieden werden soll, um dem künftigen, politisch anders zusammengesetzten Senat nicht vorzugreifen.

Nur herrscht nicht überall Stillstand. Vielmehr droht Rückschritt, und zwar ganz erheblicher. Der Berliner Berufsverband Bildender Künstler (BBK Berlin) schlug jetzt Alarm . Es gingen, so hieß es in einer Stellungnahme, nach und nach zahlreiche Atelierräume verloren, weil die entsprechenden Generalmieter – die für das Land Berlin die konkrete Raumbewirtschaftung betreiben – aufgrund finanzieller Unsicherheiten auszuscheiden drohen oder bereits ausgeschieden sind.

"Bisher keine erkennbare Lösung"

"Seit November 2024 reißen die Hiobsbotschaften nicht ab", machte der BBK Berlin am 16. November auf die schleichende Demontage aufmerksam: "Zunächst wurde im Zuge der Kürzungen des Nachtragshaushalts auch die (...) Abwicklung der Kulturraum Berlin gGmbH angekündigt – der Trägerin des Arbeitsraumprogramms und Generalmieterin von rund einem Drittel der Atelierhäuser und zahlreichen Orten der Darstellenden Künste, Literatur, Musik und Projekträume. Wenig später folgten fortlaufend Kürzungen des Arbeitsraumprogramms um mittlerweile mehr als 50 Prozent, ausbleibende haushaltspolitische Freigaben und damit fehlende Perspektiven für langfristige Mietverträge. Auch für die angekündigte Herausnahme der vier GSE-Treuhandobjekte aus der Förderung fand die Verwaltung bislang keine erkennbare Lösung.“

Es ist nicht ganz einfach, sich durch die Zahlen zu arbeiten, die rund um die Ateliersituation erhoben werden und greifbar sind. Das Kulturwerk des BBK Berlin hat zuletzt im Sommer 2023 "Basisdaten zur Bedarfserhebung der Ateliersituation bildender Künstler*innen" vorgelegt, die man ohne weiteres auf den gegenwärtigen Zustand fortschreiben kann.

Seinerzeit waren bei der Künstlersozialkasse (KSK) 14.000 Künstlerinnen und Künstler gemeldet und versichert, davon rund 8500 "vorwiegend im klassischen Selbstauftrag wie Malerei, Bildhauerei, Installation". Die Datenerhebung des Verbands haben seinerzeit nur eine Minderheit von 1673 Künstlern beantwortet. Auf deren ausgefüllten Fragebögen basieren die Zahlen. Sie sind also mit einer statistischen Fehlertoleranz zu betrachten.

Verdreifachung, und trotzdem Mangel

Aber sie geben die allgemeine Tendenz wieder. Danach waren 42 Prozent der Auskunftgebenden ohne Atelier, weitere 21 Prozent sahen sich bedroht oder bereits mit Auszug konfrontiert. Auf der anderen Seite gab es zu diesem Zeitpunkt nicht weniger als 1214 geförderte Atelierräume, mehr als eine Verdreifachung in den zurückliegenden beiden Jahrzehnten.

Diese Zahl blieb einigermaßen konstant; zum Jahresende 2024 „befanden sich 1924 durch das Land Berlin geförderte Arbeitsräume in Nutzung“, wie die Sprecherin der Senatskulturverwaltung, Britta Elm, auf Anfrage von Monopol mitteilte: "Hiervon sind 1199 den Ateliers der Bildenden Kunst zuzuordnen."

Insgesamt wurden im Jahr 2025 für das Arbeitsraumprogramm von ursprünglich 24,17 Millionen Euro nach der Kürzungsrunde noch 19,17 Millionen Euro im Landeshaushalt ausgewiesen. Dieser Posten ist im folgenden Doppelhaushalt für 2026 mit 20,446 Mio. Euro und für 2027 mit 19,263 Mio. Euro beziffert. Hinzu kommen Investitionen "für den Ausbau von Arbeitsräumen für Künstlerinnen und Künstler" in Höhe von 3,85 Millionen Euro für beide Haushaltsjahre. In einer Vorlage für den Hauptausschuss des Abgeordnetenhauses vom 26. März 2026 erklärte die Kulturverwaltung jedoch kategorisch, eine Erweiterung des Atelierbestands sei "derzeit nicht darstellbar".

Von gesichert bis ganz verloren

Im Netz ist eine interaktive Karte einsehbar, die die Verteilung der geförderten Räume über ganz Berlin wiedergibt, zusammen mit der jeweiligen Anzahl von Ateliers. Hervor sticht der Bereich in Tempelhof nahe der Stadtautobahn. Hier befinden sich in ehemaligen Gewerbebauten 76 Ateliers in der Gottlieb-Dunkel-Straße und 32 in der Schätzelbergstraße, aber auch 36 in der Teilestraße, die nur bis Ende kommenden Jahres gesichert sind.

Ebenso das Atelierhaus in der Neuköllner Schönstedtstraße mit 30 Ateliers, aber auch einem Programm an Veranstaltungen für die Öffentlichkeit. Langfristig gesichert sind die 23 Ateliers in der Kienitzer Straße in einem, so der BBK, "wunderschönen, kernsanierten Hinterhof-Fabrikgebäude". Also eine Top-Adresse.

Ganz verloren ist hingegen das Atelierhaus in der Sigmaringer Straße in Wilmersdorf, das in dieser Innenstadtlage 26 Räumlichkeiten bereithielt. Noch sind die entsprechenden "schwarzen" Punkte auf der Karte in der Minderzahl. Der BBK Berlin hatte auf Grundlage seiner Erhebung von 2023 gleich 3500 Ateliers gefordert. Auf Dauer.

Situation "nicht länger tragbar"

Drängend ist das Problem des Rückzugs von Generalmietern. Zuletzt hat die Gesellschaft für StadtEntwicklung gGmbH (GSE) ihren Ausstieg aus dem Atelierraumprogramm angekündigt.

In ihrer Stellungnahme vom 20. November erläutert die GSE gegenüber Monopol ihre bisherigen Aufgaben: "Als freier Träger übernimmt die GSE bis heute die organisatorische und kaufmännische Betreuung der Räume im Arbeitsraumprogramm. Dazu gehören das Vertrags- und Mietenmanagement, Raumübergaben sowie die Koordination notwendiger Reparaturen und Handwerksarbeiten. Eine zentrale Aufgabe ist außerdem die Bewirtschaftung der Fördermittel gegenüber der Senatsverwaltung für Kultur und Gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt. Diese Abrechnung über die sogenannte projektbasierte Fehlbedarfsfinanzierung ist mit erheblichen bürokratischen Anforderungen und finanziellen Unsicherheiten verbunden. Zunehmend besteht das Risiko, dass Kosten, die der GSE tatsächlich entstehen, wie beispielsweise Mietzahlungen an Eigentümerinnen und Eigentümer, nicht vollständig als förderfähig anerkannt und erstattet werden. Damit trägt die GSE finanzielle Risiken, die sie als freier Träger nicht dauerhaft auffangen kann. Angesichts langfristiger Verträge mit Zahlungsverpflichtungen in siebenstelliger Höhe ist diese Situation für die GSE nicht länger tragbar."

Die Schlussfolgerung aus "unkalkulierbaren finanziellen Risiken" ist deutlich: "Deshalb steht die GSE als Zuwendungsempfänger für das Arbeitsraumprogramm zukünftig nicht mehr zur Verfügung." Das bedeutet keinen sofortigen Bruch, schließlich sind langfristige Mietverträge zu erfüllen. Der Berlin-Stadtplan des BBK zeigt denn auch weit mehr gesicherte als gefährdete oder demnächst aufgegebene Räumlichkeiten.

"Weiter intensiv einsetzen"

Es handelt sich jedoch vielmehr um einen schleichenden Erosionsprozess. Zwar beruhigt die GSE fürs Erste: "Bis zum Auslaufen aller aktuellen Hauptmietvertragslaufzeiten bleiben wir daher weiterhin eine verlässliche Partnerin an der Seite der Künstlerinnen und Künstler im Arbeitsraumprogramm."

Auf Anfrage von Monopol äußerte sich die Senatskulturverwaltung zurückhaltend. In ihrem Schreiben vom 25. November geht Pressesprecherin Britta Elm nicht näher auf die – gleichfalls nicht genau spezifizierten – Vorhaltungen der GSE ein: "Mit dem Raum- und Budgetwachstum der vergangenen Jahre sind die Anforderungen an das Förderprogramm stetig gewachsen. Die Komplexität des ARP hat deutlich zugenommen." Ob nur die Zahl der geförderten Räume gewachsen oder auch deren Verwaltung tatsächlich "komplexer" geworden ist, bleibt ohne Erläuterung. Es folgt jedenfalls Zustimmung zu der Ansage der GSE, dass es nicht weitergehen könne wie bisher: "Die Verwaltung und Bewirtschaftung von Liegenschaften (ergo: Hausverwaltung) mittels einer Projektförderung ist weder zeitgemäß noch sachgerecht."

Was das konkret für die Bewilligung und Auszahlung der Fördergelder bedeutet, muss wohl nach Maßgabe der künftigen Spitze des Hauses ausgehandelt werden. Die Senatssprecherin beruhigt derweil mit den Worten: "Unser Haus – und das gilt sicher auch für die potentielle Nachfolger:in – wird sich weiterhin intensiv für den Erhalt des Raumportfolios einsetzen." Was nochmals unterstreicht, dass in der gegenwärtigen Übergangszeit bis zur Bildung des neuen Senats nichts mehr entschieden wird.

Die Uhr läuft weiter

Doch ohne eine grundsätzliche Neugestaltung der Fehlbedarfsfinanzierung und ihrer konkreten Abläufe seitens des Senats wird sich an der Schieflage nichts ändern. Der noch amtierende Kultursenator heißt Stefan Evers (CDU), der als Finanzsenator die Kultur seit dem Rücktritt der von der CDU nominierten Sarah Wedl-Wilson im April 2026 lediglich mitbetreut.

Wer in einer möglichen künftigen rot-grün-roten Koalition zuständig sein könnte, ist derzeit nicht absehbar. Auf eine Anfrage von Monopol hat die Senatsverwaltung bisher nicht reagiert. Das klingt nach Stillstand – aber die Uhr läuft weiter. Seine besten Zeiten hat das Berliner Atelierprogramm womöglich hinter sich.

article_text:
O n 8 December last year, the great director Rob Reiner signed off the prologue for Who Killed JFK? , his book written with David Hoffman and Dick Russell and based on his podcast with Soledad O’Brien. Describing a lifelong fascination with the assassination of John F Kennedy in Dallas on 22 November 1963, and what he saw as the vast conspiracy to cover up who really killed the 35th president, Reiner wrote: “Maybe, people don’t truly want an answer. Perhaps we are safer not knowing … Well, I’m done being safe.”

Six days later, Reiner and his wife, Michelle Reiner, were stabbed to death in their home. Charged with murder, their son Nick Reiner has pleaded not guilty .

Reiner’s other son, Jake Reiner, “actually read the prologue for the audiobook”, Hoffman said. “Like his father, he’s got this incredible voice but he’s also a performer … He just did such a great job, and it was hard to not be emotional. The last sentence and then the date of it … really, it strikes you as to how poignant and meaningful it is. And obviously, nobody knows better than Jake how important this was to Rob.”

Reiner was 15 when Kennedy was killed. Russell was the same age and developed the same fascination. The author of 16 books, including studies on Kennedy, he was a researcher and commentator for the Who Killed JFK? podcast. In book form, Russell, Reiner and Hoffman, an author, historian and screenwriter, tell the story of the killing and the shadow it cast.

Hoffman said: “There is just so much intrigue, so many personalities, so many natural cliffhangers that make you want to turn the page … So the question was: ‘How do we take something that is so complicated and distill it in a way that feels definitive, but also feels as though someone who might not know a ton about the JFK assassination is enthused to keep going. This is where having Rob Reiner on the team certainly comes invaluable.”

The director of Misery, A Few Good Men and more “was a master storyteller”, Hoffman said, “and one of the things I have learned is that the best storytellers, one of their great talents is knowing what to leave on the editing-room floor. So I think between the three of us – Dick knowing everything there is to know, a full encyclopedia about the JFK assassination, Rob one of the world’s all-time great storytellers, and me somewhere kind of in the middle, trying to put those pieces together – we complemented each other.”

Russell said that even though he had “been deep in the weeds of this for 50 years off and on”, he “learned a lot still and it was amazing to work with Rob and David … and by the end of it, we wanted to be able to convince readers there was a lot more to this than investigations had shown.”

About those investigations. First there was the Warren Commission , established by JFK’s vice-president, Lyndon B Johnson, and chaired by chief justice Earl Warren, reporting in September 1964. Then there was the US House select committee on assassinations , which reported in 1979 after three years’ work. There have been file releases since, notably under Donald Trump . Debate over who killed Kennedy will never end.

The official version is that Kennedy was shot by Lee Harvey Oswald , a young drifter with leftwing links who was himself killed two days later by Jack Ruby, a Dallas nightclub owner. Reiner, Hoffman and Russell do not agree. Who Killed JFK? considers what the authors say are many holes in the case against Oswald, and the suspects for an alternative explanation: the CIA and FBI, the mob, US and Cuban rightwingers. Combinations of all three. At the book’s end, the authors identify men they say carried out the assassination itself.

Russell said: “It was a matter of following threads and piecing together what we could from what exists, and we discovered that an awful lot was on the record but was ignored by the Warren Commission and to some degree by the House committee as well. And these were people who are in the literature, so to speak. We talked to some of them.”

The book admits that JFK research “is filled with Rorschach tests”, evidence or events in which any reader might see something different. A whole section is called The Wilderness of Mirrors. Hoffman said: “I think our challenge was, when you look at the JFK assassination, it is not an investigation or a mystery where there is a lack of information. The issue is you are opening up a jigsaw puzzle that’s 63 years old. You realize there’s supposed to be 1,000 pieces here and a bunch of them are missing. You start to go through it. You realize a bunch of these pieces don’t belong in here … So you start to think, ‘Which pieces do fit together?’ [JFK author] Jefferson Morley calls it fact patterns. We thought of clusters of information. When we found clusters that pieced together cleanly, that gave us confidence that was something we could build upon.”

Russell said: “There were some very interesting and dramatic things that we had to leave out because we couldn’t fit them into that framework comfortably, meaning, ‘Does this move the narrative forward, but also, is it true …’ That was Rob’s eye, a lot of the time, saying, ‘God, I really think this is probably true, but we don’t have enough to prove it, and so we’ve got to leave it on the cutting room floor.’”

Hoffman said: “It was very intentional that none of this is built upon a piece of evidence or a single witness or anything like that. When you step back, there’s just a ton of information … whether it’s Oswald being connected to intelligence or any of the other key tenets of the case that we build.”

Rather than examine each reason Hoffman, Russell and Reiner believe Oswald did not kill JFK, that he was a patsy caught in a plot, I posit just one point. Dominic Sandbrook, co-host of the hugely popular The Rest Is History podcast, thinks Oswald acted alone. One point of evidence cited by Sandbrook is that Oswald was an excellent marksman, trained in the US marines, certainly capable of making the fatal shots from the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository. Reiner, Russell and Hoffman, however, write that Oswald was a terrible shot, citing a Marine Corps nickname based on shooting test scores – “Shitbird” – and the testimony of another enlistee. So what would Hoffman and Russell say to Sandbrook?

“I had a copy of the book on me the other day,” Hoffman said, “and I went to a coffee shop in Los Angeles. A guy came up to me and said he was a marine for 20 years, and he goes, ‘I don’t know what that book says, but Oswald was a terrible shot. There’s no way he could have done that. I’m telling you, as a marine.’ So it’s funny you bring this up, three days later.

“The marksman thing is completely misleading. A marksman is not a high rank in terms of people that are capable with a rifle. It’s not a terrible rank, but it sounds to a layperson, ‘Wow, that person must be really good with a rifle.’ But marksman is not one of the highest rankings you can get on those tests … That’s one. Two is I think that test was in 1958 or ’59. There is virtually no record that is reliable of [Oswald] firing a gun, practicing with a rifle in the ensuing four years. So if you take someone that in 1959 was a mediocre shot, give him a gun that everyone acknowledges is an absolute piece of junk, he hasn’t practiced in four years, and put him in that building, that is not a shot that you would assume someone like him would make.”

On the gun, Russell expanded the point: “We emphasized the fact that in the beginning, the rifle that was found there on the sixth floor was identified as a German Mauser, not a Mannlicher-Carcano , which was really not the kind of rifle you’d use to shoot someone from on high … it just didn’t have the ability to do it. A Mauser did. So that was one thing, and then of course there’s the palm print that was found on the rifle … [it] looks very likely that it was placed there later to make it look like Oswald was holding that particular rifle, which changed by the way the next day. Suddenly it wasn’t a Mauser any more; it was a Mannlicher.

“And then, of course, we looked deeply into where was Oswald at the time; what do various people say? Was he really up there? Well, some people saw two shooters, one holding a rifle. And we looked at where Oswald was even before he went to his rooming house and ended up in the Texas theatre,” where he was arrested on 22 November 1963, initially for the murder of the Dallas police officer JD Tippit. “You know, people saw him in the lunchroom. He said he was in the lunchroom, having a Coke.”

Like Reiner, Hoffman and Russell do not think the evidence against Oswald adds up.

Who Killed JFK? is out now .

article_text:
Keanu Reeves is set to star in Maelstrom , a new Netflix action flick from Carry-On ‘s Jaume Collet-Serra, sources have confirmed to Deadline.

Reeves takes over the lead from Reacher ‘s Alan Ritchson, who exited the project for undisclosed reasons. Reps for Netflix declined to comment.

In Maelstrom , a Federal Marshal assigned to protect the fiancée of an arms dealer turned witness must defend her through one brutal night as a hurricane cuts off communication, strands them without reinforcements, and unleashes the dealer’s men on their safe house.

Related Stories

Reed Hastings On Netflix Shakeup, YouTube Rivalry And How Streamer Can Go Back To "Being Thrilling"

Ted Sarandos Shrugs Off U.S. Troubles To Mark Netflix's 10 Years In Korea

The current draft of the script is by Mark Bianculli; the first draft was by the late Gregory Fitzpatrick. This is one of those projects that has been working its way through the system for many years, having first been set up as a spec at Warner Bros. back in 1993.

Watch on Deadline

Jeff Robinov will produce alongside Tabitha Shick and Talking Pictures.

Coming off the fourth installment of his John Wick franchise, Reeves has been aggressively expanding his slate of late. Most recently, he entered talks to lead James Wan’s take on South Korean crime actioner The Gangster, The Cop, The Devil for Paramount, where he’s also set to reprise his voice role of Shadow in Sonic the Hedgehog 4 . As we first reported, Reeves recently set up an adaptation of the forthcoming Oliver Lowe novel Kill Current: A Jon Hendricks Thriller as another starring vehicle. That film will mark the first project produced under his new banner Two Dragonflies. His partners are The Arena and Zando.

Other upcoming projects for Reeves include the Warner Bros. sci-fi flick Shiver and The Entertainment System Is Down , from multiple Palme d’Or winner Ruben Östlund. Page Six Hollywood announced his Maelstrom casting.

article_text:
À 20 ans seulement, ELLIE avance à contre-courant. Autrice et compositrice, la jeune niçoise à la présence charismatique s’éloigne du cadre académique et se met à composer depuis sa chambre d’adolescente, avec pour seuls compagnons GarageBand et son téléphone. Dans un monde en perpétuel mouvement, elle prend le temps et se démarque avec des singles comme « In the Breach » et « On My Own », écrits en anglais pour dompter sa nature réservée, puis son EP Invisible Things, dans lequel la chanteuse multi-instrumentiste fait cohabiter des élans de rock avec des piano-voix.

Pour son premier clip Here Down on Earth , produit par le studio Remembers, on retrouve l’idée de la “chambre-refuge” : elle nous fait entrer dans un rêve (ou serait-ce un cauchemar ?) de 3 minutes, mêlant cinématographie, archives et créations 3D. On passe d’un champ de blé, à une cabane faite de bois dont le toit est recouvert de pans de draps. Une silhouette se découpe sur le crépuscule, les ailes déployées : comme un retour à la danse, discipline qui a formé la chanteuse aux boucles brunes. Puis la cabane protéiforme émerge d’un brouillard blanc traversé de faisceaux de lumière, avant que les flammes ne l’engloutissent, dans un incendie qui rappelle celui du Sacrifice d’Andreï Tarkovski.

Dans le même temps, la Terre s’embrase, comme pour signifier que c’est notre maison au sens large qui est menacée. Le clip s’achève sur la cabane ressuscitée, et la voix d’ELLIE, profonde et enveloppante, semble nous dire qu’une lueur perce peut-être l’obscurité.

article_text:
Jordan Firstman knew that the success of “ Club Kid ” hinged on finding the perfect preteen actor to play his character’s long-lost son, Arlo.

It was a demanding role that had a lot of boxes to check off: A British kid, whose hard-partying mother had just committed suicide, finds himself dumped in New York City, where he struggles to break out of his protective shell to bond with his party promoter dad, Peter (Firstman, who wrote and directed the film , in addition to starring in it ). But the perfect candidate had to project an effortless coolness that allows him to organically blend in with his newfound father’s social circle of hard-living, LGBTQ+ clubgoers, whose lives revolve around their love of music, dance, and drugs.

“[Arlo’s] not just cool, he’s empathetic and wise; there’s a lot of stuff about that kid that was on the page that needed to be there,” said Firstman, who on this week’s episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast , called the casting search the most “nerve-wracking” part of making “Club Kid.”

“Club Kid” had the right casting director for the job. Carmen Cuba has a legendary track record of finding child stars, including the original “Stranger Things” ensemble. But as Cuba pointed out while participating in IndieWire’s Craft Roundtable of Casting Directors , “Club Kid” was different from those previous assignments.

“I do six-month searches for kids,” said Cuba. “On ’Stranger Things,’ ‘Starfighter,’ you have time and money, and this was a small film.”

The $6 million production could not afford a lengthy search. It didn’t even have the money for Cuba to fly to London with Firstman for auditions. She would be reliant on a UK casting team, working within a limited budget, to help her find a needle in a haystack. “I was very nervous about just sort of the plan of attack, because I was going to have a UK team, and you need a British kid who looks like he’s half-Jordan,” said Cuba.

Right before jumping into “Club Kid,” Cuba went on her yearly vacation with a group of close casting director friends. As the holiday wound down, Cuba tried to work through her upcoming casting dilemma with some of her closest colleagues.

“I [said], ‘How am I going do this?’ just trying to map it out for myself before I left to go start it,” recalled Cuba of the conversation. “And one of those friends is Lucy Bevan, who had just finished her ‘Harry Potter ’ search.”

To cast the first season of the $200 million-plus upcoming HBO series — based on the first Harry Potter book, “The Philosopher’s Stone,” in which Harry turns 11 — Bevan had just finished her own six-month search. She had auditioned thousands of young British actors to play the next generation of Harry, Hermione, Ron, and their Hogwarts classmates.

“This is just a testament to our relationship because Lucy would not normally do UK casting on a tiny movie,” said Cuba of the prominent British casting director, whose credits include “Barbie,” “F1,” and “The Batman.”

“She had just seen 40,000 kids,” said Firstman of Bevan, who early on showed him a photo of Reggie Absolom. “I saw his face and I was like, ‘that is the face that I’ve seen in my head.’ Even in the script, he’s supposed to be a quarter Indian – ‘Innit Babes’ [Peter and his friends’ nickname for Reggie’s mom based on her favorite expression] is supposed to be like half Indian — and Lucy [said], ‘Let’s not focus on that. That’s not going happen.’ And Reggie’s a quarter Indian. Every single thing that I had asked God for, this kid came to me in Reggie.”

In total, according to Cuba, Bevan showed Firstman 90 kids, with a wider range of ages — Cuba and Firstman went back and forth about how old Reggie should be, with the character originally skewing younger than 10 — but Firstman never wavered from Absalom, whose résumé included roles in “Silo” and “The Other Bennet Sister.”

“Lucy was so generous. They had no money to fly me to London to do the session in person, so she hosted the callback session there,” said Cuba. “Jordan is incredible with kids, he was like, ‘Let’s not do it in this casting office, let’s take it outside.’ So suddenly Lucy’s assistant is outside with the camera, and they’re walking and talking. I rewatched that audition recently, and it’s just amazing. Jordan’s brain, and how he connects to everyone that he casts. I think that’s what you feel in the movie; it’s so familial.”

On the podcast, Firstman talked about how beyond his decade of drug-fueled clubbing in Europe and New York City, one of the inspirations for “Club Kid” was the bond he formed with one of his close friend’s child, something he felt would be essential to replicate with Absolom.

“The reason kids like me is I don’t treat them as kids,” said Firstman. “They’re surprised at my candor, or the inappropriate things that most adults wouldn’t be willing to say in front of a kid. I know what Reggie sees on the internet. I’m not going to say something too much, but I can push it a little bit. I think he always appreciated that in me, and once he understood that I liked to be made fun of too, everything shifted. Once he got permission to make fun of me, the whole dynamic shifted, and we just got so much more comfortable around each other.”

Much like his unorthodox, take-it-outside, walk-and-talk callback audition with Absolom, Firstman quickly realized, after casting the young actor, traditional preparation wouldn’t work.

“We tried doing traditional rehearsals, and it was awkward,” said Firstman. “I [said], ‘Let’s just keep hanging out, and keep having pizza together, and keep talking about music, and keep talking about TikTok clips we’ve seen, and send each other TikToks,’ and that’s how we bonded.”

An A24 release, “Club Kid” is now in New York City and Los Angeles theaters, and will expand on Friday, November 13.

article_text:
“ Gondhal ,” the Marathi-language thriller India has put forward for the international feature Oscar at the 99th Academy Awards, has launched its global trailer as its awards push moves into a new phase.

The film is the first feature from writer-director Santosh Davakhar. It was chosen from a field of 33 films in contention for India’s submission.

The story plays out over a single night in rural Maharashtra, during a Gondhal, a folk ritual in which devotion is expressed through song, dance and theatrical storytelling. Ishita Deshmukh plays Suman, a young wife stuck in a suffocating marriage. She tries to take back control by playing on the fixation her lover Sarjerao (Nishad Bhoir) has developed for her. As her desires run up against codes of honor and custom, the night ends in tragedy.

Related Stories

A Cyclops on Strings and Samantha Morton Reshaping Faces by Hand: How Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Made Its Monsters Real

Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Overtakes ‘Avatar: The Way of Water’ as Korea’s Biggest International Film of All Time (EXCLUSIVE)

Kishor Kadam, Yogesh Sohoni and Anuj Prabhu also star. Amalendu Chaudhary shot the film, which opens with an unbroken take lasting 25 minutes. Legendary composer Ilaiyaraaja wrote the music and background score.

“Global perceptions of Indian cinema are often shaped by narratives of poverty and caste conflict – important realities, but not the complete expression of India,” said Davakhar. “India is also a civilization of extraordinary cultural wealth, sustained by traditions, music, and collective memory. I created this film to bring one such powerful tradition to the global screen through a culturally authentic and universal cinematic language.”

Davakhar won the Silver Peacock for best director at the 56th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Jury members at the festival called the film “like a Shakespearean fable set in a real world.”

Davakhar produced the film with Diksha Davakhar, his co-founder at production banner Davakhar Films. The company backs regional stories and aims for top-tier craft in camera work, sound, music and acting.

Ferrero）内揭幕。这个全新的阅读、学习和聚会空间献给这位在2025年逝世、曾将论文研究聚焦于加利齐奥（Gallizio）的评论家兼策展人，它源于一项由“造作银行”——矩阵基金会（Banca del Fare – Fondazione Matrice）、读者圈基金会（Fondazione Circolo dei lettori）以及阿尔巴市民共同参与的共创规划过程。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在公共艺术方面，由 CRT 艺术基金会（Fondazione Arte CRT）构思并支持、与 CRC 基金会（Fondazione CRC）合作并由玛尔塔·帕皮尼（Marta Papini）策划的第四届“拉迪斯”（Radis）项目，计划在卡纳莱（Canale）市镇实施一项全新的特定场域（site-specific）艺术介入。该作品交由一位其姓名尚未公布的国际艺术家创作，并将伴随展览、教育活动以及与当地社区的会面。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在阿尔巴的皮耶罗·马塞拉（Piero Masera）街区，则将成形由伊拉里奥·伊索拉（Hilario Isola）构思、保拉·尼科林（Paola Nicolin）策划并与“林荫中”（Nel Viale）协会合作的“拉尔斯”（I Lari）项目。该介入受保护家庭与城市空间的古老伊特鲁里亚-罗马神祇“拉尔斯”（Lari）启发，计划在与医生兼摄影师皮耶罗·马塞拉的生活相关的地点放置一系列永久雕塑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这一年中，公众还可以在每周六参观瓦莱里奥·贝鲁蒂（Valerio Berruti）的工作室，他是放置在米歇尔·费雷罗广场（piazza Michele Ferrero）的雕塑《阿尔巴》（Alba）的创作者。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/03-alba.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "阿尔巴市，c. article_text:
Dalla riscoperta di Pinot Gallizio attraverso una mostra diffusa curata da Maurizio Cattelan e Marta Papini , all’eredità critica di Roberto Longhi , fino alla nascita di una nuova manifestazione internazionale a cadenza biennale, passando per progetti di arte pubblica, festival, interventi permanenti e programmi educativi. È stato presentato il 27 novembre 2026 alla Triennale Milano Le Fabbriche del vento , il programma ufficiale di Alba Capitale italiana dell’arte contemporanea 2027 , che coinvolgerà, oltre alla città piemontese, il territorio di Langhe, Roero e Monferrato. La manifestazione prenderà il via con un fine settimana inaugurale, dal 29 al 31 gennaio 2027, e si svilupperà lungo tutto l’anno, con iniziative a ingresso gratuito.

Promosso dal Ministero della Cultura, attraverso la DGCC – Direzione Generale Creatività Contemporanea, e dal Comune di Alba, il progetto è realizzato dall’Associazione Le Fabbriche del vento, presieduta da Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo , con la direzione artistica di Nicolas Ballario . Alla presentazione sono intervenuti anche Costantino D’Orazio , direttore generale Creatività Contemporanea del Ministero della Cultura, e Alberto Gatto , sindaco di Alba.

Il titolo del programma, ispirato a due opere dell’artista albese Pinot Gallizio (1902-1964), rimanda all’intenzione di costruire un sistema culturale diffuso, nel quale l’arte contemporanea possa entrare in relazione con le specificità sociali, produttive e paesaggistiche del territorio, generando nuove progettualità destinate a proseguire oltre l’anno della Capitale.

Maurizio Cattelan e Marta Papini rileggono l’opera di Pinot Gallizio

Tra gli appuntamenti centrali del programma inaugurale figura Quasi un autoritratto , mostra diffusa dedicata a Pinot Gallizio, curata da Maurizio Cattelan e Marta Papini in collaborazione con l’Archivio Gallizio, in programma dal 30 gennaio al 20 giugno 2027.

Farmacista, erborista, partigiano, protagonista dell’avanguardia europea del dopoguerra e tra i fondatori dell’Internazionale Situazionista, Gallizio rappresenta uno dei principali riferimenti attorno ai quali è stato costruito il programma di Alba Capitale. La mostra ne ripercorrerà la figura attraverso alcune delle sue opere più significative, distribuite in diverse sedi cittadine legate alla biografia e all’attività dell’artista.

A confrontarsi con la sua eredità saranno sei artisti contemporanei di diverse generazioni e provenienze: Simnikiwe Buhlungu , attraverso la sperimentazione sonora; Roberto Fassone , con la dimensione performativa; Katharina Grosse , attraverso la pittura immersiva; Ragnar Kjartansson , indagando le relazioni tra arte e teatro; Goshka Macuga , in dialogo con la figura dello stesso Gallizio; Małgorzata Mirga-Tas , attraverso la sua ricerca sulla narrazione per immagini.

Alla figura di Gallizio sarà dedicato anche Alba zona libera dell’antimondo , un itinerario situazionista proposto dal Centro Studi Beppe Fenoglio, in collaborazione con le istituzioni culturali cittadine e gli studenti delle scuole superiori. Dal 30 gennaio il percorso accompagnerà il pubblico alla scoperta dei luoghi, degli oggetti e delle relazioni che scandirono la vita dell’artista.

Il dialogo con il Mozambico e la mostra di Francesco Vezzoli su Roberto Longhi

Sempre durante il fine settimana inaugurale, dal 30 gennaio al 4 aprile 2027, Palazzo Mostre e Congressi Giacomo Morra ospiterà Radici contemporanee / Raízes contemporâneas , esposizione dedicata al dialogo tra una nuova generazione di artisti e curatori mozambicani e figure italiane dell’arte, della critica e della ricerca.

La mostra restituirà gli esiti di Italia – Mozambico. Un ponte fatto ad arte , progetto di cooperazione culturale promosso dal Ministero della Cultura, attraverso la Direzione Generale Creatività Contemporanea, l’Unità di Missione per la cooperazione culturale con l’Africa e il Mediterraneo allargato e i Musei Nazionali di Perugia – Direzione regionale Musei nazionali Umbria, insieme all’Ambasciata d’Italia a Maputo.

In autunno sarà invece la Fondazione Ferrero a promuovere uno dei principali appuntamenti espositivi dell’anno: Francesco Vezzoli. La Discoteca di Roberto Longhi , mostra curata da Arturo Galansino con Simone Facchinetti .

Il progetto metterà in relazione la pratica artistica di Francesco Vezzoli con l’eredità critica dello storico dell’arte Roberto Longhi , nato ad Alba nel 1890. Attraverso sette secoli di arte italiana, ripercorsi a partire da opere e artisti scoperti, studiati o valorizzati da Longhi, la mostra indagherà l’attualità del suo metodo interpretativo, mettendolo in dialogo con i processi di appropriazione e rielaborazione delle immagini del passato che caratterizzano la produzione di Vezzoli.

Alba Capitale oltre Alba: le iniziative nelle Langhe, nel Roero e nel Monferrato

La dimensione territoriale rappresenta uno degli assi portanti del programma, che intende coinvolgere anche i piccoli centri, le realtà produttive e le comunità locali.

Il progetto Capitali Sorelle riunirà le iniziative dei partner del circuito Orma – Resté, Germinale, La collina sale sempre, Creativamente Roero e Associazione Sindaci del Roero – insieme a quelle di numerosi comuni delle Langhe, del Monferrato, del Roero e di alcuni centri della Liguria, selezionati attraverso un’apposita open call. Mostre, eventi e percorsi di arte pubblica entreranno così a far parte del palinsesto ufficiale della Capitale.

Dal 1° maggio al 28 novembre 2027 si svilupperà invece Vigne ad Arte , progetto curato da Costanza Vilizzi che porterà opere d’arte contemporanea all’interno delle cantine e dei ristoranti del territorio, affiancando agli interventi artistici un programma di visite, incontri ed eventi dedicati alle relazioni tra paesaggio vitivinicolo, cultura enogastronomica e ricerca contemporanea.

A favorire ulteriormente la partecipazione delle realtà locali sarà il Circuito EXTRA , una rassegna aperta alle proposte di associazioni, spazi indipendenti, scuole, fondazioni, operatori culturali, attività commerciali e singoli cittadini interessati a sviluppare progetti nell’ambito delle arti visive.

Il lascito di Alba Capitale: una mostra internazionale biennale dal 2028

Uno degli obiettivi più ambiziosi della candidatura riguarda la nascita di una nuova manifestazione internazionale d’arte contemporanea a cadenza biennale, concepita per coinvolgere stabilmente le Langhe, il Roero e il Monferrato a partire dal 2028.

Il progetto sarà presentato nell’autunno del 2027, nell’ambito di un convegno dedicato alla futura manifestazione. Nelle intenzioni dei promotori, la biennale dovrà costituire il principale lascito dell’anno della Capitale, dando vita a un’istituzione culturale permanente, fondata sul rapporto con il territorio e sulla costruzione di una rete internazionale di collaborazioni.

«Con Alba Capitale abbiamo cercato di sfuggire alla logica del grande evento che si insedia in un luogo e lo consuma per poi lasciarlo», ha dichiarato Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, sottolineando la volontà di costruire un programma capace di lasciare in eredità alle comunità nuove produzioni artistiche, competenze, pubblici e relazioni tra soggetti pubblici e privati.

La Biblioteca Luca Beatrice e i progetti di arte pubblica

Tra i lasciti permanenti della manifestazione figura anche la Biblioteca Luca Beatrice, che sarà inaugurata il 29 gennaio 2027 all’interno della Biblioteca Civica G. Ferrero di Alba. Dedicato al critico e curatore scomparso nel 2025, che aveva incentrato proprio su Gallizio la sua ricerca di tesi, il nuovo spazio di lettura, studio e incontro nasce da un processo di progettazione partecipata che ha coinvolto Banca del Fare – Fondazione Matrice, Fondazione Circolo dei lettori e i cittadini albesi.

Sul versante dell’arte pubblica, la quarta edizione di Radis , progetto ideato e sostenuto dalla Fondazione Arte CRT in collaborazione con Fondazione CRC e affidato alla curatela di Marta Papini, prevede la realizzazione di un nuovo intervento site-specific nel Comune di Canale. L’opera, affidata a un artista internazionale il cui nome non è stato ancora annunciato, sarà accompagnata da mostre, attività educative e incontri con la comunità locale.

Nel quartiere albese di Piero Masera prenderà invece forma I Lari , progetto ideato da Hilario Isola e curato da Paola Nicolin , in collaborazione con l’associazione Nel Viale. Ispirato alle antiche divinità etrusco-romane protettrici degli spazi domestici e urbani, l’intervento prevede la collocazione di una serie di sculture permanenti nei luoghi legati alla vita del medico e fotografo Piero Masera.

Durante l’anno sarà inoltre possibile visitare, ogni sabato, lo studio di Valerio Berruti , autore della scultura Alba , collocata in piazza Michele Ferrero.

Arte contemporanea, sostenibilità ambientale e salute

L’Ospedale Michele e Pietro Ferrero di Verduno sarà uno dei luoghi in cui si svilupperà il dialogo tra arte, ambiente e salute. Il progetto Arte per la Riforestazione – Bosco del Cambiamento , realizzato in collaborazione con l’Associazione Arte Continua, prevede la piantumazione di alberi nelle aree verdi della struttura ospedaliera, attraverso una raccolta fondi sostenuta dalla vendita di opere di artisti contemporanei, tra cui Antony Gormley , Tobias Rehberger , Carsten Höller e Leandro Erlich .

Proprio l’ospedale ospiterà, già dal 10 dicembre 2026, un’installazione del progetto Luci d’Artista , a cura di Antonio Grulli , realizzata in collaborazione con la Fondazione Ospedale Alba-Bra. L’intervento costituisce uno degli appuntamenti di avvicinamento all’anno della Capitale e anticipa ulteriori installazioni luminose previste tra la fine del 2027 e l’inizio del 2028.

Teatro, danza, cinema e design nel programma di Alba Capitale 2027

Il programma si estende anche alle arti performative con Per.Forma , festival dedicato all’incontro tra teatro, danza e arte contemporanea, in programma dal 1° al 4 aprile 2027. Gli appuntamenti si distribuiranno tra il Teatro Sociale G. Busca, la Chiesa di San Domenico, le piazze cittadine e luoghi generalmente estranei ai circuiti della performance, come i ristoranti La Piola e Piazza Duomo della famiglia Ceretto.

Dal 1° al 5 settembre il Cortile della Maddalena ospiterà invece Vision , rassegna cinematografica realizzata insieme a Sky Arte, con cinque serate di proiezioni all’aperto accompagnate da incontri con artisti e protagonisti del mondo dell’arte contemporanea.

Alla cultura del progetto sarà dedicata Design Gallery , nuovo spazio espositivo promosso da Gruppo Sereno in collaborazione con Italian Radical Design. Al centro del percorso saranno le produzioni di marchi come Gufram, Memphis e Meritalia, che tra gli anni Sessanta e Ottanta contribuirono a ridefinire i confini tra arredamento, scultura e arte contemporanea. A questo nucleo si affiancheranno, attraverso allestimenti a rotazione, opere e oggetti di aziende come Edra, Knoll, Flos e Kartell.

Il confronto tra arte e altri ambiti del sapere caratterizzerà infine Ricalcolo , public program ideato da Nicolas Ballario che metterà gli artisti in dialogo con figure provenienti dal mondo della scienza, dell’artigianato, dell’impresa, dell’agricoltura, della musica, della filosofia e della cucina.

«L’ambizione è che l’arte diventi una presenza quasi accidentale nella quotidianità delle persone, che la si possa incontrare anche senza aver deciso di cercarla», ha spiegato il direttore artistico.

Il programma educativo per coinvolgere 5mila studenti

A sviluppare il programma educativo e di mediazione culturale sarà il Dipartimento educativo della Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, in collaborazione con quelli della Fondazione Ferrero e del Museo Civico Eusebio.

A partire da febbraio 2027 saranno proposte visite e attività laboratoriali gratuite rivolte alle scuole di Alba e del territorio, con l’obiettivo di coinvolgere circa 200 classi e 5mila studenti. Il progetto contribuirà inoltre alla formazione di giovani educatori e mediatori culturali locali.

In collaborazione con l’ASL CN2 Alba-Bra, alcune attività saranno rivolte anche a persone con fragilità, pazienti oncologici, anziani e caregiver, sperimentando forme di integrazione della partecipazione culturale nei percorsi di cura.

Alba Capitale italiana dell’arte contemporanea 2027 potrà contare sul sostegno di Regione Piemonte e Provincia di Cuneo e su una rete di partner pubblici e privati, tra cui Fondazione Ferrero, Fondazione CRC, Fondazione Arte CRT, Miroglio Group, Banca d’Alba, Fondazione Circolo dei lettori, Ceretto e Iren.

article_text:
For almost eight decades the artists’ model Louise Cansot, the subject of the novel winning France’s most prestigious literary prize this year, was one of Paris’s forgotten murder victims.

After her body was found near the Seine in September 1949, city police wrote off the young woman, immortalised as “the girl of 100 portraits”, as loose, libertine and – worse – an unmarried mother. They closed their investigation after just four months having made little effort to find her killer.

But long before the author Philippe Jaenada began researching his, Prix Goncourt-winning novel , L’ Inconnue du Quai de Javel (The Unknown Woman of the Quai de Javel) , another writer from the Breton village where Cansot was born had already spent decades researching her story.

Luc Corlouër might have felt aggrieved but in a rare show of literary solidarity, the two writers decided they would both publish books. As part of what he calls “the deal”, Corlouër handed Jaenada his notes.

“We agreed we would write our respective books, which are very different. And after all, the star was him, not me,” Corlouër told the Guardian. “By giving him the subject I knew he would make a really superb book. He is a great novelist.”

Cansot, nicknamed Lise, was born in Tréguier, on the Côtes-d’Armor in north-west France, the daughter of a shoe repairer. In 1937, aged 16, she left her family and moved to Paris where her beauty attracted the attention of the celebrated Montparnasse artists, who jostled to have her pose for them.

When war broke out and most of the artists fled south, Cansot remained in Paris working as a film extra, waiter and dancer at the Folies Bergère. She had a five-year-old daughter, Nathalie, whom she left with a nanny in the suburbs until she could raise the money for an apartment, but with the painters gone and no steady income, her situation became increasingly desperate.

On 7 September 1949, her body was found on the Quai du Javel, now known as the Quai André-Citroën, in the 15th arrondissement, south-west of the Eiffel Tower. Detectives initially identified four possible murderers but rapidly filed the case as unsolved.

Jaenada, the author of 17 novels, discovered the story while looking through old newspapers in the French National Library.

By then, Corlouër had already amassed maps, images, photos, paintings, documents, letters and newspaper cuttings on Cansot. His book, La Tragédie du plus beau modèle de Paris (The Tragedy of the Most Beautiful Paris Model) was finally published on 19 August – the same date as Jaenada’s novel – and is based on the documentary information about the case and the victim.

Corlouër says his interest in Cansot was piqued in 1981, when he met an elderly woman at the war memorial in Tréguier. “She told me one name was of a local girl, Annick Cansot, run over by a German truck during the war. When I said: ‘How terrible,’, she said even worse was that her older sister had been murdered in Paris.

“I decided I had to know about Louise Cansot and what happened to her, so I began researching, but my book was a failure. It was a novel about a murder investigation that did not identify the murderer. It was rejected by one publisher after another.

“I thought there was only one person capable of writing such a book: Philippe Jaenada, whom I had already met at a literary salon. Then one day he contacted me. He told me he was interested in the case but said he wouldn’t do anything without me.

“So, I entrusted him with my research. I gave it to him and he did the best investigation imaginable. He dissected all the information and found things I didn’t even think of.”

The original 300-page police report on Cansot’s murder concluded that she was a woman of “ill repute” and newspaper reports speculated that she was a sex worker, alcoholic or drug addict.

In his 530-page book, Jaenada gives a more sympathetic portrayal of the victim, and suggests the name of the man he believes strangled Cansot after inviting her to visit a flat she hoped to rent. His research included reading 74 out of the 75 novels by Georges Simenon featuring Inspector Maigret in 1940s Paris.

Corlouër said it was unsurprising the police had not made the same effort to find the killer back then.

“Lise was a very modern girl at least 50 years ahead of her time,” he said. “She dressed well, was intelligent and free in her choice of lovers. But when she was killed, what journalists and the police saw was a young woman who was a bit libertine, had a baby out of wedlock, had jobs they didn’t think were proper jobs and posed for painters. To them, she had brought what happened on herself.”

Corlouër said he and Jaenada had wanted to rehabilitate Cansot’s reputation after 77 years of slander. “In the police report it’s more or less written that she deserved it. And the defamation continued after her murder,” he said.

Corlouër also revealed how the authors traced Cansot’s daughter Nathalie, now 80, who was raised by another sister, Valentine.

“I don’t want to say too much because it would spoil the end of Philippe’s novel, but when we found her, the first thing she said was she didn’t want to hear a word about her mother and that Lise was a prostitute,” Corlouër said.

“She was raised by her aunt, who was very jealous of Lise and who for years told the girl her mother was disreputable. Nathalie was very surprised when Philippe and I told her this was not true, that her mother was an amazing woman.

“When she heard this, she did not cry. She’s tough like her mother, but she was amazed. So there is a kind of happy ending to this tragic story.”

article_text:
Art Movements

Print Center and Women’s Studio Workshop Name New Leaders

Plus, SITE Santa Fe artists announced, awards for Lorna Simpson and Wolfgang Tillmans, and Penske Media partners with Amazon … because of course.

Art Movements, published every Thursday afternoon, is a roundup of must-know news, appointments, awards, and other happenings in today’s chaotic art world.

Yukiko Yamagata to Helm NYC's Print Center

New York's Print Center, home to programs and exhibitions celebrating all the art that's pressed, proofed, and published, announced Yukiko Yamagata as its new executive director this week.

Her professional profile doesn't immediately scream “print nerd”: Yamagata most recently served as deputy director at Creative Time and previously worked at the Open Society Foundations, where she led a $15.8 million arts and culture fellowship program for socially engaged artists. But one of her earliest roles in the 1990s was as a senior curatorial assistant in the photo department at the Whitney Museum of American Art, and she is a current board member of Women Photograph, an organization focused on equitable practices in photojournalism and visual media.

Yamagata succeeds Judy Hecker , who announced her decision to step down earlier this year after a decade in the role, and is now executive director emerita.

Natalie Renganeschi to Lead Women's Studio Workshop

The Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, New York, dedicated to the printing arts as well as papermaking, bookbinding, photography, and more, has named Natalie Renganeschi as its fourth-ever executive director in the organization's 52-year history.

Renganeschi's career at WSW began in 2018, when she joined as a part-time employee while working as a high school art teacher. Now, she will oversee the nonprofit's major campus expansion, including the relaunch of its ceramics center.

“My path to leadership hasn’t been a traditional one, but it’s rooted in the ethos of WSW,” Renganeschi said in a statement. “Just as our mediums are steeped in process and the history of craft, working here is a sustained act of communal learning that allows for growth to come from below and within.”

article_text:
Issue

One on One: Kimsooja on John Cage

JOHN CAGE ’s statement at the Paris Biennale, 1985. Courtesy Kimsooja Studio.

It is difficult for me to identify a single artist as the source of my artistic inspiration, yet if I had to name someone whose thinking greatly inspired my understanding of what art could be, it would be John Cage.

I first encountered Cage’s work at the Paris Biennale in 1985. I entered a white railway container expecting a sound installation; instead, I found an almost empty space and a statement, written in French along the corner of the floor: “ Que vous essayez de le faire ou pas, le son est entendu (Whether you try to make it or not, the sound is heard).” The encounter was immediate, revealing, and profound. I recognized Cage as a master—not because I wanted to follow his artistic language, but because his proposition articulated something fundamental: the world does not wait for the artist to make it exist; the artist simply creates the conditions through which we become attentive to it.

This realization resonated deeply with questions that I was exploring in my practice, and later became central to my approach of “non-doing” and “non-making.” These ideas do not mean an abstinence from action or making. Rather, they involve minimizing the artist’s intervention so that phenomena already present—light, sound, gravity, movement, reflection, breathing, and the passage of time—can reveal themselves. In this sense, the artist’s role is less about producing something new than creating a state of heightened perception.
excerpt_original: The Korean artist recalls how John Cage informed her understanding of what art could be, describing her first encounter with his work in 1985. Kimsooja

article_text:
Lionsgate and Steven Paul ‘s SP Media are launching a new joint venture which will have the latter making a capital investment that will allow the former to continue its diversification of 3 Arts and other new businesses.

At the same time, the deal calls for SP Media to produce independent features films that Lionsgate will distribute. Lionsgate will have the majority stake in the joint venture, and will manage it.

Note, Paul is not becoming a minority investor in Lionsgate overall, rather a co-financier in the j.v. With Lionsgate, SP gains a distributor for its feature slate.

Related Stories

Lionsgate Stock Jumps On Report Of Takeover Offer By Legendary

'La La Land' Stage Musical Taps Film's Choreographer & Costume Designer; 59 Studio Aboard As Production Designer

The news comes at an interesting time with Legendary in due diligence with Lionsgate after sending the corporation a takeover offer last Tuesday. Sources tell Deadline that no formal process is underway for Lionsgate to accept acquisition offers; meaning no bankers have been hired.

Watch on Deadline

Paul is the chairman, founder and CEO of Crystal Sky Pictures and SP Media Group, and has shepherded such franchises as Baby Geniuses , as well as Ghost Rider and Ghost Rider 2: Spirit of Vengeance , starring Nicolas Cage, Ghost in the Shell , starring Scarlett Johansson, and the Lionsgate-distributed Rambo: Last Blood .

SP Media Group President & COO Scott Karol and Paul, are special advisors to Donald Trump Hollywood Ambassador Jon Voight, and have been working with federal lawmakers and industry groups on bipartisan legislation aimed at creating a U.S. film and TV tax credit and curbing runaway production.

In the summer of 2024, when David Ellison’s Skydance was pursuing Paramount, Paul spearheaded a group of investors that included John Paul DeJoria, the billionaire co-founder of Patron tequila and Paul Mitchell hair care products, to make a $2.25 billion offer for National Amusements Inc., the Redstone family holding company that owned 77% of Paramount’s voting stock.

“Steven is a savvy & experienced entrepreneur who has a longstanding relationship with our studio, and I’m pleased to partner with him across multiple touchpoints of our business,” said Lionsgate CEO Jon Feltheimer. “He recognizes the unique and valuable assets that we have built and his investment will help drive the continued growth of these businesses.”

“Lionsgate is one of the most dynamic and entrepreneurial content studios in the media space today,” said Paul. “I’m delighted to build on my longstanding relationship with Jon Feltheimer and the Lionsgate leadership team as we grow our businesses together in an industry environment filled with opportunity.”

The joint venture deal with SP Media was negotiated for Lionsgate by COO Brian Goldsmith, EVP & General Counsel Bruce Tobey, and Senior VP Corporate Development Suzy Felfeli and for SP Media by Karol. Moelis served as financial advisor to Lionsgate and Lazard served as financial advisor to SP Media. Paul Hastings LLP represented SP Media on the deal.

Jill Goldsmith contributed to this piece.

Hyperallergic )

For more than two decades, one question has followed me since I was abused by Jeffrey Epstein: “Why me?”

In trying to understand what happened, I have come to recognize that the answer lies not only in the manipulation I endured, but also in the institutions and social structures that helped make that manipulation possible.

Leon Black’s board position at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) is one of the starkest examples of institutional ignorance — a head-in-the-sand, look-the-other-way mentality that will inevitably give abuse of power a dark corner to grow and fester in.
